title: Langflow unauthenticated RCEs exploited in the wild but not in CISA KEV; Metasploit ships six Langflow modules
why: VulnCheck and F5 Labs report in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-0768, and it is not in CISA KEV. The KEV feed added only the PHP CVEs on Oct 26. Metasploit added Langflow modules on Oct 23. Not re-searched this run. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Take Langflow off the internet (put it behind a VPN or auth proxy), set a non-default secret key, disable AUTO_LOGIN, and rotate every secret configured in flows.
product: Langflow up to 1.4.2 unauthenticated; code exec persists in later versions with default AUTO_LOGIN (no complete fix per Pruva)

title: Magento PolyShell unauthenticated file upload: mass-exploited since March (953-store loader campaign), public PoC, no CISA KEV listing
why: Sansec reports PolyShell mass exploitation since March 2026 (471 stores infected in one hour) and an ongoing loader campaign across 953 stores. A public PoC is on GitHub. No KEV listing appears, and the KEV feed added only the PHP CVEs on Oct 26. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Apply APSB26-73, deny all access to pub/media/custom_options/, then audit the cms_block table, admin users and the filesystem for loaders, webshells and GSocket backdoors.
product: Adobe Commerce / Magento Open Source 2.4.9, 2.4.8-p5, 2.4.7-p10, 2.4.6-p15, 2.4.5-p17, 2.4.4-p18 and earlier (fixed by 2026-jul isolated patch, APSB26-73)

title: Splunk Enterprise unauthenticated RCE via Patroni REST API on search head cluster members: public PoC with mass-exploit mode
why: A public GitHub PoC (Patroni PATCH /config archive_command + restart) includes check and mass-exploit modes. Splunk makes no exploitation statement and the CVE is not in CISA KEV. The same sidecar had a KEV-listed flaw in June. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Upgrade to Splunk Enterprise 10.4.3/10.2.7. If you cannot, set [postgres] disabled = true (when Edge Processor/OpAmp/SPL2 are unused) and firewall Patroni to SHC peers only.
product: Splunk Enterprise 10.4.0-10.4.2 and 10.2.0-10.2.6 search head cluster members (fixed 10.4.3 / 10.2.7); 10.0.x and 9.4.x not affected

title: Pillow EPS/Ghostscript argument injection to command execution (CVSS 9.2), fixed in Pillow 13.0.0
why: The advisory includes a public reproduction. Not in CISA KEV and no in-the-wild reports as of Oct 23. Not re-searched this run; the KEV feed added only the PHP CVEs. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Upgrade Pillow to 13.0.0+ and remove Ghostscript from image-processing hosts that do not need EPS.

title: Linux kernel skb_zerocopy local root (ZDI-CAN-33367): public PoC bypasses Dirty Frag fix; fix still unmerged, no CVE
why: A working root PoC is public (TuxCare, CloudLinux and Sysdig). The netdev patch has been reviewed and tagged for stable but is still not merged. There is no CVE, it is not in CISA KEV, and no in-the-wild use has been reported. AlmaLinux kernels are in testing and KernelCare livepatches are rolling out.
action: Block the esp4/esp6 modules or set user.max_user_namespaces=0 where possible, and install distro kernel or livepatch updates as they ship.
product: Linux kernel since 3.14 (skb_zerocopy), incl. kernels with Dirty Frag CVE-2026-43284 fix

title: CERT-UA: Dahua cameras/NVRs compromised via Easy4IP serial guessing plus old KEV auth bypasses (CVE-2021-33044/33045)
why: Not ahead: CVE-2021-33044/33045 have been in CISA KEV since 2024.
action: Disable P2P/Easy4IP on Dahua devices, update the firmware, and remove unknown user accounts.
product: Dahua IP cameras and recorders with pre-mid-2021 firmware and Easy4IP P2P enabled

title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply-chain compromise: Microsoft publishes analysis (Storm-0940); LiteLLM blames key exposed in May
why: No longer ahead: Microsoft Security published a technical analysis on Oct 23 attributing the compromise to Storm-0940, so Microsoft is tracking it.
action: Find any install of litellm==1.107.0 or its images and rotate every credential reachable from those hosts.

title: Unpatched Linux KSMBD RCEs (ZDI-CAN-33774 pre-auth, ZDI-CAN-33549 SMB Direct, CVSS 9.0) public on LKML with no mainline fix
why: Detailed ZDI reports leaked to public LKML. There is no mainline fix (only a maintainer-tree commit) and no CVE, and the flaws are not in CISA KEV. Public PoCs show only crashes and leaks.
action: Unload/disable ksmbd where not needed and block TCP 445 from untrusted networks.

title: HPE Aruba AOS-8/AOS-10: eight max-severity unauthenticated auth-bypass/RCE flaws among 72 CVEs (HPESBNW05162)
why: A vendor advisory covers max-severity unauthenticated flaws in widely deployed edge gear. No PoC or in-the-wild use yet, and not in CISA KEV. Not re-searched this run.
action: Upgrade AOS-8/AOS-10 controllers and gateways to the fixed releases and restrict management interfaces.

title: NGINX heap overflows/UAF (CVSS4 9.2) allow unauthenticated DoS and possible RCE in specific configurations
why: F5 advisory K000163408 and an oss-security disclosure. No in-the-wild use, no public PoC, not in CISA KEV. Not re-searched this run.
action: Upgrade NGINX to 1.30.6/1.31.7 (or F5 fixed builds) and review configs with nginx -T for alias/map/aio usage.
product: NGINX Open Source before 1.30.6 / 1.31.7; NGINX Plus 37.0.0-37.0.4; Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, Instance Manager

title: Apple backports exploited CoreGraphics zero-day fix (CVE-2026-86950, KEV) to iOS/iPadOS 18.7.11 in Oct 26 updates
why: Already in CISA KEV (added Sep 29), so not ahead.
action: Push iOS/iPadOS 18.7.11 to devices that cannot run iOS 26/27 and the Oct 26 updates to everything else via MDM.
product: iOS/iPadOS before 18.7.11 (older devices, e.g. iPhone XS/XR) and before 26.7.1; macOS Tahoe before 26.7.1, Sequoia before 15.8.1

title: Apache Traffic Server: unauthenticated ImageMagick argument injection in experimental magick plugin (CVSS 10) among 15 ATS fixes
why: Apache's Oct 21 advisory discloses an unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaw. No PoC or in-the-wild use, not in CISA KEV. Not re-searched this run.
action: Upgrade ATS to 9.2.16/10.1.5/10.2.1 and disable the magick, tsmemcache and wasm experimental plugins if not needed.

title: FortiSandbox GUI unauthenticated auth bypass to command execution (CVSS 9.6, vendor E:F)
why: Fortinet FG-IR-26-185 and ZDI-26-771 describe the flaw, and Fortinet's vector carries E:F, but no public exploit has been found. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Upgrade FortiSandbox to 5.0.7 or 4.4.10 and restrict the management GUI to admin networks.

title: Tailworm: unpatched Tailscale SSH socket-forwarding flaws let one compromised node reach root on other tailnet servers (vendor acknowledges, no fix)
why: Erica Windisch published 11 lab-reproduced findings on Oct 25, and Tailscale acknowledged them. As of Oct 26 there is no bulletin, CVE or release, though a commit moving socket forwarding out of root tailscaled was merged on Oct 26. Not in KEV, and no in-the-wild use.
action: Disable forwarding in Tailscale SSH rules, use per-pair source-to-destination grants, enable Tailnet Lock, and watch Tailscale bulletins for the release.
product: Tailscale 1.104.2 (tested) with Tailscale SSH enabled; headscale 0.29.5

title: Wasmtime Cranelift sandbox escapes from malicious Wasm modules (CVSS 9.9, two CVEs)
why: Maintainer advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0379/0380). Not in CISA KEV, with no PoC or exploitation reported.
action: Rebuild every program that embeds Wasmtime against 36.0.19, 48.0.7 or 49.0.4. Updating the CLI is not enough.

title: Rust zip crate (through 9.0.4): central-directory vs local-header filename confusion lets crafted archives evade inspection (CVSS 10.0)
why: Newly published in NVD (Oct 26) with a CNA CVSS of 10.0 for a heavily used Rust crate. No PoC, no in-the-wild use, not in CISA KEV. Only one source, so confidence is low.
action: Find zip <= 9.0.4 in Cargo.lock files (cargo-audit) and update when a fixed release is listed. Until then, do not mix ZipArchive inspection with ZipStreamReader extraction.
